summary: Backend: 10/11 pytest cases pass (90.9%). Content shape, encounter rules (gargoyle advance/death/keyword/help), the_unmade (step1 'no' wins; step0 'raise lantern' with lit_lantern advances), telemetry, admin stats and 404 all pass. One minor parser edge case failed: 'asdf qwrt' is not classified as absurd because 'asdf' contains vowel 'a' - the gibberish detection skips short words lacking vowels but accepts any word with a vowel. Falls through to intent=talk and still returns result=stay with fallback text, so functional behavior ('stay' + hints) is preserved. Frontend: title screen, NEW GAME, scene transitions, hotspot pickups (coin/lantern), locked-sunbeam-until-tree-inspected gating, taken_text + no-duplicate on re-click, puddle death + reload-checkpoint restoring to scene entry, save/CONTINUE round-trip after page reload, help modal open + Esc close, toggle-hotspots-button, mute-button, Bram dialogue (4 choices, keyboard shortcut '1' advances to sub-choices), inventory panel structure, mobile 390px layout (no horizontal overflow, pack within border) all work. cliff_fall.jpg asset exists and is wired into guard/throne death effects in content.py. Did not full-run guard death / twins / ending interactive flow via Playwright because main agent already verified happy path end-to-end; focused on edge cases per request.

minor.issue: Input 'asdf qwrt' is NOT flagged as absurd (because 'asdf' contains vowel 'a'); gibberish heuristic in parser.py only triggers when ALL words >2 chars lack vowels. Behavior still returns result='stay' via intent='talk' fallback, but absurd_text branch is not exercised. Consider using stricter heuristic (e.g., consonant-cluster ratio or dictionary check) if the spec requires absurd detection on inputs like 'asdf qwrt'.

action_items: Optional: tighten parser absurd/gibberish heuristic so inputs like 'asdf qwrt' are classified as absurd per spec. Low priority — functional behavior (stay+fallback) is unchanged.
critical_code_review_comments: parser.py gibberish detection only fires when every word>2 chars lacks a vowel; single vowel in one short token bypasses it. Spec expects 'asdf qwrt' to be absurd.
server.py uses deprecated FastAPI @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') — consider migrating to lifespan context managers (non-blocking, modern style).
server.py seed_content() injects '_id' into dict with keys that may conflict with model fields — currently harmless because strip_id removes before response, but worth noting.
seed_data_creation: None - backend content is auto-seeded by server on startup
context_for_next_testing_agent: Pytest file at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py covers content shape, both encounters, telemetry, admin stats, 404. Known minor: TestEncounterGargoyle::test_absurd_stays asserts absurd==True on 'asdf qwrt' and fails because parser accepts 'asdf' (has 'a'). To make test pass, either (a) relax assertion to just check result=='stay', or (b) tighten parser. Use truly consonant-only strings like 'bzzz qrs tzz' to reliably trigger absurd branch. Frontend data-testids are stable; dialogues block hotspot clicks (expected), so close dialogue (choose 'Back to business' / 'Leave') before clicking hotspots again.
rca of the issue: parser.py line 62: `gibberish = not any(len(w) > 2 and re.search(r"[aeiouy]", w) for w in words)` — the predicate inside any() is True when a word is >2 chars AND contains a vowel. 'asdf' is 4 chars and has 'a', so any() returns True → gibberish=False → absurd=False. Fix: require ALL non-trivial words to look pronounceable, or use len(word)>=2 && has consonant-cluster-ratio>0.7, or maintain a short wordlist/profanity+common-verb set.
